query: I have a brand-new NestJS app and want to add nest-profiler. Where do we start?
expected_behavior: Must start by introspecting the project (package manager from the lockfile, package.json dependencies, whether production code calls the profiler API such as TracerService / @Span(), the entrypoints main.ts / app.module.ts / a CLI, DI-injected loggers, the build setup) before writing any code. Must NOT jump straight to pasting a ProfilerModule snippet.

End-to-end setup. Nothing calls the profiler API, so recommend the dev-dependency install (first option, '(recommended)' on the label). Install with pnpm's dev flag: 'pnpm add -D @eleven-labs/nest-profiler nestjs-cls @eleven-labs/nest-profiler-typeorm' (typeorm/@nestjs/typeorm stay production dependencies). Create profiling/profiling.module.ts with ProfilerModule.forRoot({ isGlobal: true }) + TypeOrmCollectorModule (optionally TypeOrmSchemaCollectorModule) — NO inject: [DataSource] (it self-resolves via connectionName) and nothing added to the feature modules. Add app.dev.module.ts, a shared bootstrap.ts, main-dev.ts wrapping the logger with the standalone createProfilerLogger (no TracerService), the tsconfig.build.json exclusions + tsconfig.dev.json and the start:dev script on --entryFile main-dev. No PROFILER_ENABLED, no ConditionalModule. Verify the dev entry (X-Debug-Token, /_profiler) and the production build after a production-only install (/_profiler 404).

query: My app already has ProfilerModule wired up and I just added @nestjs/cache-manager. How do I add cache profiling?
expected_behavior: Recognize the core profiler is already configured and this is adding a single collector — route the user to the add-nest-profiler-collector skill rather than running a full setup.

Recognize this is NOT a NestJS application (no @nestjs/core; plain Express). nest-profiler targets NestJS 11+ on Node 22+, so it does not apply. Should not wire ProfilerModule; instead explain the requirement and ask the user to confirm it is a NestJS app.

Introspect and detect multiple relevant collectors: nest-profiler-cache (hard peer @nestjs/cache-manager) and nest-profiler-auth (heuristic via @nestjs/passport/@nestjs/jwt). Must ASK the user (multi-select) which detected collectors to add rather than assuming all. Wire core + logger and register the chosen collectors in the ProfilingModule bundle (cache requires CacheModule.register({ isGlobal: true }) in the app), installed with the same flag as the core, and state that the default install keeps the profiler out of production (without stating it as an absolute ban).

query: I'm wiring log capture for the profiler. What exactly goes in the entrypoint?
expected_behavior: With the dev-dependency install, in main-dev.ts only (production main.ts never references the profiler): create the app with { bufferLogs: true }, then app.useLogger(createProfilerLogger(new ConsoleLogger('App'))) — typically through the shared bootstrap's wrapLogger hook — importing the standalone createProfilerLogger from @eleven-labs/nest-profiler. Must NOT resolve TracerService for logging: createProfilerLogger is DI-free (reads the active profile from CLS) and a transparent pass-through when the profiler is off. Services should log with new Logger(Name); a directly-injected logger (e.g. PinoLogger) needs the optional LOGGER_WRAP seam filled by the dev bundle (or createProfilerLogger at its injection point with the ConditionalModule install).

query: package.json includes @nestjs/common, @nestjs/core and @nestjs/config. User: My API is internal only, reachable through our VPN, and I understand the exposure. I want the profiler enabled in production too, not just in dev.
expected_behavior: Must NOT flatly refuse. Respect the informed explicit choice (internal API behind a VPN, risks understood) while noting it is off-by-default for good reason. Help them harden it per references/core-options.md (or route to the harden-for-production skill): the profiler is open by default so provide a `security` strategy (reuse an app guard via `security.guards`, or an `authorize` predicate) for /_profiler, keep collectBody: false, lower sampleRate and cap maxProfiles/ttl, add ignorePaths/ignoreRequest for sensitive routes, and mind file/sqlite persistence. Can still use PROFILER_ENABLED so it stays toggleable. Must NOT reference a built-in token/PROFILER_TOKEN (removed).

Dev-dependency install (the recommended default). Install with the dev flag: 'pnpm add -D @eleven-labs/nest-profiler nestjs-cls'. Keep production main.ts + AppModule profiler-free; move the bootstrap into a shared bootstrap.ts; create a dev-only AppDevModule (imports AppModule + ProfilingModule) booted only by main-dev.ts, which wires createProfilerLogger (and createProfilerValidationPipe if the validator collector is added). No ConditionalModule/@nestjs/config, no PROFILER_ENABLED gate, no ProfilerNoopModule, no env-condition helpers. Exclude the dev files from tsconfig.build.json, add tsconfig.dev.json and 'start:dev': 'nest start --watch --entryFile main-dev -p tsconfig.dev.json'. Verify BOTH: dev entry boots with /_profiler, and the production build boots after a production-only install (no MODULE_NOT_FOUND, /_profiler 404).

Introspection finds production code calling the profiler (TracerService injection). Present the install choice in fixed order (dev dependency first, labeled recommended) but explain in option 2's description that it is the one that fits, since the dev-dependency install would leave the TracerService import unresolved in production. With option 2: 'pnpm add @eleven-labs/nest-profiler nestjs-cls @nestjs/config', env-condition helpers, ConditionalModule.registerWhen(ProfilingModule, isProfilerEnabled) + ProfilerNoopModule.forRoot({ isGlobal: true }) on not(isProfilerEnabled), createProfilerLogger in main.ts, PROFILER_ENABLED=true in .env for local dev only.
